notes:
Spec asserts: a synchronous slash command renders locally with no model call, so state stays ready and no →working transition fires for the slash itself. For copilot the mechanism is the CLEANEST of the three shapes seen so far: the TUI's slash dispatcher handles the input and returns {handled:true} without ever entering the prompt path that emits user.message (app.js ~7800573), and /usage's action is an add-timeline-entry that resolves to the React timeline's addEphemeralEntry (~8516764/~8634781) — in-memory UI state. CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-08-03 (CLI 1.0.77): across the whole /usage window the session's events.jsonl gained NO line at all (the transcript goes assistant.turn_end → session.shutdown with nothing between) and the daemon emitted no state_transition, so the session sat continuously ready for ~13 s. Contrast claudecode (a <local-command> wrapper its parser must filter) and aider (the slash logged as a real user prompt, which does flicker working). Belt and braces: every event type other than user.message and assistant.turn_end is Skip in core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go, so even a stray lifecycle line in the window could not move state.

The warm-up turn goes FIRST and is mandatory — copilot writes events.jsonl only once the first prompt lands, so without it there is no real session to assert against.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED from the live recording: the transient proc-<PID> row is born ready and is the presession anchor, but the REAL session is born DIRECTLY into working (state_transition new_state=working, reason "new session created") because events.jsonl already carries the open warm-up turn when the daemon first sees it. Session birth and warm-turn start are therefore ONE phase; the pre-recording spec asserted a ready birth followed by a separate ready→working, a shape that does not exist.

OBSERVATIONS: the warm-up turn supplies live tokens and cost (session.shutdown's cumulative modelMetrics block — session.usage_checkpoint carries no counts); model is NOT pinned because --model accepts only "auto" and session.auto_mode_resolved picks per turn.
